Compiler.note: BW-03 batch B, --size-param 0 (n=5000000). buildIR_validPhi_go is a SINGLY-recursive chain (no branching children), so oracles/compiler_model.py does one forward iterative pass mirroring the build order exactly, instead of recursion (n reaches ~6.4M steps including PHI insertions, past Python's default recursion limit) or memoization (no benefit for a linear chain). Cross-checked at a reduced n=3000 against the real compiled program first (exact match on all 11 fields), then at the full n=5000000 scale (exact match). Unlike List.hs/LinearListReduction.hs (VW-33), this ~6.4M-deep non-tail recursion does NOT segfault under --use-mutable-cursors -- confirmed by running the byte-identical pre-width-migration source (HEAD plus the pre-existing badPhis-returns-Int restructuring) at the full size before touching anything, and it completed normally. Opcode 6 (PHI) is provably confined to positions where verifyPhiPlacement_IO's seenNonPhi is freshly reset, so badPhis is provably always 0, confirmed by direct simulation (not copied from the observed output). Migrated output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-migration program's output; AoS and SoA also match each other exactly. 'expected' includes two prefix lines the driver's semantic-output filter does not strip: the intro `Running the Compiler IR Program:` (does not match the `Running program ...:` protocol pattern -- wrong wording) and a stray `End: ` (with colon) printed once after the throughputModelPass pass only -- a pre-existing source quirk (every other pass prints bare `End`, which IS filtered), unrelated to width migration and identical in both AoS and SoA. See the PiecewiseFunctions entry's note for the general prefix-matching issue this uncovered across the batch. KDTree.note: BW-03 batch C -- the owner-designated explicit-Int64 program (every other curated program is explicit Int32; KDTree.hs's ADT fields were changed from bare `Int` to explicit `Int64`, a pure width-declaration change with no value-level effect, since bare `Int` already meant Int64 in this dialect). --size-param 0 (d=22, axis=0). buildKD recurses with the IDENTICAL (d-1, nextAxis) on both children, so every reduction pass's l/r (or dl/dr, ml/mr, hl/hr) subtree results are always equal at every node -- confirmed from the source's own comment ('computed unconditionally for Gibbon compiler stability') -- so oracles/kdtree_model.py collapses each pass to one recursive call per level (memoized by (d,axis[,phases,rays,seed,radius])) instead of a naive two-branch simulation. Leaves are built only at d==0, where buildKD ignores axis entirely, so every leaf is identical: point (0,1,2), mass 0, objectId 0 -- this makes sumMassInRange provably 0 for every query (proved by induction: leaf mass is always 0, so ml=mr=0 at every level, hence every combination is 0), confirmed against the compiled output. dist/corrCount/cloudCount were also independently hand-derived analytically (not just simulated) before running the model, all matching. Cross-checked the full model at a reduced d=6 against the real compiled program (exact match on all 6 fields) before trusting it at the full d=22 scale (also exact match). All photonMappingBenchmark divisions have provably non-negative operands throughout the recursion, so no truncating-division helper is needed here (unlike DecisionTree.hs/DBQuery.hs). Migrated output is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the pre-migration program's output; AoS and SoA also match each other exactly.

OctTree_sumMass.note: BW-03 batch D, --size-param 0 (d=8, seed=17). Shared oracles/octtree_model.py: buildOctree gives each of its 8 children a DIFFERENT seed (mixSeed seed 1..8), so unlike KDTree.hs there is no shared-subtree collapse -- the model materializes the real ~19M-node tree (8^8=16777216 leaves) once and reduces over it directly. `mixSeed`'s Int64 arithmetic wraps (ctypes.c_int64, as in trie_model.py), and buildOctree's `p`/`v` leaf fields apply `mod` to a value that can be negative post-wrap, needing the `tmod` truncating-remainder helper (discovered here the same way DecisionTree.hs's was: a small-scale d=1 cross-check against the real compiled program mismatched until corrected). sumMass never reads a Cell's own cached fields -- it recurses to Particle leaves and sums their `mass` field directly -- so it is UNAFFECTED by the newly-discovered defect documented on countActive/sumEnergy below. Exact match against the real compiled program at both d=1 and the full d=8. OctTree_fmmPotential.note: BW-03 batch D, --size-param 0 (d=8, probe=21, order=4, eta=70). Value UNCHANGED by BW-03.1.1's strict-Int32 migration despite `fmmPotential`/`fmmUpSeries`/`fmmDownSeries` (and their `probe`/`order`/`eta` parameters) all moving from Int64 to native Int32 -- re-verified, not assumed: the model was independently re-derived from scratch with `wrap32` applied to every Int32 op (`oracles/octtree_model.py`'s `fmm_potential`/`fmm_up_series`/`fmm_down_series`) and reproduces 229379432 exactly, then cross-checked against a fresh, forced recompile of the real program (both AoS and SoA agree). This is a STRUCTURALLY ABSORBED case, the same pattern documented on ColorOctree's `energy`: the only nodes with `m` large enough for `m*100`/`m*c` to actually overflow Int32 are near the root, where `s` (halfSize) is also large, making `farLhs = s*100` big enough that the far/near opening test (`farLhs < farRhs`) almost always chooses to RECURSE rather than take the `approx` short-circuit at those nodes -- so the overflow-prone multiplication is never actually evaluated on a large `m` in the reachable computation, in either width. Historical: originally BLOCKED by VW-24 (real output 0), FIXED in Phase 8 step 2. ColorOctree.hs has its own SEPARATE local ADT (not OctTreeBase's), but the same seed-divergent-8-children build shape, so oracles/coloroctree_model.py materializes the real ~19M-node tree once and reduces both passes over it directly. Every semantic integer is now genuinely Int32 (owner policy: no Int64 exception for overflow alone), with wrap32 applied after every add/sub/mul in the model, mirroring Gibbon's own C-level wraparound exactly -- including `sr+sg+sb` (used by `energy`), which genuinely overflows Int32 (~6.4e9 at the root) and changes `energy`'s underlying value at every node where sr/sg/sb are large. Despite that, the FINAL observable tuple is unchanged from the pre-strict-Int32 value: verified independently (the Python model reproduces the identical tuple both before and after adding wrap32) and confirmed directly against the real compiled program's actual output. The reason is structural, not coincidental: `energy` only affects `paletteEntriesQuantized`'s decision at nodes with `lvl < maxDepth` (4), and at every such shallow node in this committed tree, the separate `compact*(1+cnt/16) < threshold` stopping condition is already false (so the algorithm always recurses further there without ever consulting `energy`) -- `energy`'s wrapped value is only actually read at deeper nodes where `lvl >= maxDepth` already forces `approx=1` unconditionally, regardless of `energy`. `paletteEntriesQuantized`/`quantizationErrorProxy` are also now fully native Int32 (previously deferred in Phase 8 step 5 over an abundance of caution about `compact*(1+cnt/16)`, confirmed here to stay within Int32's ceiling at the committed size). Both AoS and SoA match exactly.
